title: Merge lists without counting twice
hook: Two requests overlap on three items. Adding the list lengths overcounts.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Use inclusion-exclusion for two overlapping resource lists.

misconception: The size of a merged list is always the sum of both list lengths.
objective: Use inclusion-exclusion for two overlapping resource lists.

claims.text: List A has eight distinct items; list B has six. Exactly three items occur on both lists. Scaled model; exact three-item overlap; unique items per list.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At List-A=8, A=14items and B=11items. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+","x",6]; B=["-",["+","x",6],3]; x denotes List-A. At x=8, A=14, B=11; recall at x=11: B=14. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: Count the overlap once, not twice. Adding list sizes includes the shared items in both lists, so subtract their shared count once. This assumes each individual list already has no duplicates.

At x=8, A=14, B=11; recall at x=11: B=14. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.
